# Generated files on Debian 13: effect of removal, established from public documentation

Answers: SLOWER = true cache, regenerated or bypassed with the same result; BREAKS = something stops working until an admin command or package trigger regenerates it (or the data is not regenerable); RECORD = record of the past only; UNKNOWN = documentation does not establish it.

Where no user documentation exists and the answer rests on the program's public source code or packaging scripts, the row says "(source)".

## Notes

- 1: Debian builds gdk-pixbuf with the upstream default built-in loaders (PNG, JPEG). The trixie libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-0 file list ships GIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO and other loaders as modules, which are found only through loaders.cache.
- 3: The trixie libgtk-3-0t64 file list ships im-wayland.so and im-xim.so as modules, and ibus-gtk3 ships im-ibus.so; all are found only through immodules.cache.
- 5: update-desktop-database(1) calls the file a cache that "ease[s] the work of applications". GLib's lookup, however, reads MIME associations only from mimeapps.list, defaults.list and mimeinfo.cache. For GIO applications removal therefore breaks rather than slows.
- 10a: ld.so(8) documents only /lib and /usr/lib as default paths. Debian's glibc build also compiles in the multiarch libdir (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu) as a trusted directory (debian/rules.d/build.mk, local-ld-multiarch.diff), so stock multiarch libraries still resolve without the cache. Libraries known only through ld.so.conf.d do not.
- 10b: Searched ldconfig(8) on man7.org (FILES lists only ld.so.conf and ld.so.cache) and the Debian trixie ldconfig page (HTTP 404 at the time of checking).
- 14: Debian trixie man-db ships man-db.timer and man-db.service (package file list), and the man-db postinst rebuilds index.db when it is missing.
- 15: debconf-devel(7) says a package whose only debconf use is in postrm must load its templates in postinst "Then the templates will be available when your package is being purged". Removing templates.dat breaks that case for packages that are already removed but not purged.
- 24: Running deployed apps works because the deploy directories hold hard links to the files, not because of a documented guarantee. Whether "flatpak update" works with objects missing is not documented. The documented repair path ("flatpak repair") needs root.
